thread.title: Apple just hit an all-time high (AAPL)

author: Jacob Sonenshine
title: Apple just hit an all-time high (AAPL)
text:
Tim Cook 更多 Brendan McDermid/Reuters
Apple just hit an all-time high. It's biggest conference of the year, WWDC, kicks off at 1 p.m. ET. The company has seen a recent boost from strong earnings and the belief its services business has strong growth ahead. Watch Apple trade in real time here. Apple shares hit a record high of $192.91 early Monday ahead of its biggest conference of the year . The tech giant's WWDC kicks off at 1 p.m. ET, and is expected to give updates on its big yearly software updates for iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers.
Shares had been stuck in a range between $160 to $180 for much of the past seven months before the company announced strong second-quarter results that included a hefty share buy-back plan.
Apple, classically a hardware and devices company, is in the midst of what looks to be a shift to services . In March, Morgan Stanley said it expects more than 50% of Apple's total revenue growth over the next five years to come from services. Meanwhile, it says the iPhone, which has contributed 86% of Apple's revenue growth over the past five years, will make up just 22% of that revenue growth.
Apple shares are up 11.76% this year, outperforming the S&P 500's 2.76% gain.
